note: PM refresh, 9/18. Correction made during this run: an earlier draft of this board had 'Mark Ingram' as a pursue off Kamara's Week 2 OUT designation, sourced from a web search that turned out to be unreliable -- Sleeper's own player database lists that Mark Ingram as status Inactive with no team, i.e. not a rosterable 2026 Saints player. Replaced with Kendre Miller (Sleeper-verified: RB, NO, Active), the Saints' actual depth back behind Travis Etienne, at a downgraded watch rather than pursue since the specific case for Miller inheriting touches is weaker than the retracted claim was. Also carried a correction from the AM/PM 9/17 board: Kyle Williams was priced as the Patriots' A.J.-Brown beneficiary on beat-reporter buzz, but Week 1 usage went to Mack Hollins instead (4/5 targets, team-high 51 yards, vs. Williams' zero targets on 7 routes) -- Williams drops to watch and Hollins takes the pursue spot. Two confirmed season-length openings anchor the top of the board: Higgins' torn ACL (Hutchinson) and Stribling's ~10-week ankle surgery (Robinson). No empty starting slots this week; all ten of my starters are listed Active.

targets.hook: Patriots' top target with A.J. Brown out 6 weeks
targets.why: With A.J. Brown out roughly six weeks (ankle) and Romeo Doubs/Kyle Williams unproven, Hollins posted a team-high 51 yards on 4 of 5 targets in Week 1 -- a 70% snap share and 50% route share (Yahoo Sports, 2026-09-18).
targets.asset: 70% snap share, 50% route share, 24% target-per-route-run rate, team-leading 51 yards in Week 1; profiles as Drake Maye's red-zone safety blanket for the length of Brown's absence.
targets.rate_basis: recent-trend (wk 1, first week of the expanded role)
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't beat Egbuka/Pickens for my flex, but is a clean upgrade over Kayshon Boutte on my bench -- Boutte's Houston role is now murkier (behind Collins and Hutchinson both) than Hollins' vacated-target role in New England.
targets.confidence_why: One full week of an every-down role tied to a confirmed 6-week absence, not a one-week blip -- but it's still just one game of data.
targets.competition: pauldag owns A.J. Brown and just spent FAAB on Josh Downs this week to patch his own WR corps (0 of 100 spent) -- a Patriots replacement is exactly the pickup his own roster incentivizes him to grab.
targets.bid: 10 dollars -- pauldag's price-to-beat (18) is for his top-shelf grabs; a role-replacement WR sits below that ceiling, and his hoarder-sniper tag means he's selective, not automatic, on a mid-tier name.

targets.rate_basis: recent-trend (wk 1, first game of the vacated role)
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't unseat my starters, but is a cleaner, more confirmed role than Caleb Douglas, my least-defined bench WR -- a direct swap.
targets.confidence_why: Tied to a season-ending injury (Higgins), not a game-time call, so it's durable -- but Nico Collins' own hamstring is now in question, which could push more volume Hutchinson's way or, if Collins sits, split it further with WR3 Jaylin Noel.
targets.competition: Stipe owns Nico Collins (hamstring, trending toward a Sunday absence) and has direct incentive to grab Hutchinson as his own Collins insurance -- but Stipe's tag is passive-low-ceiling despite a 23-dollar price-to-beat, so he often doesn't back real interest with a real bid.
targets.bid: 9 dollars -- enough to clear a passive bidder even with a nominal price-to-beat; his history says he underbids his own interest.
